intent: Keep a note on each confirmation saying why the owner agreed.

edit.summary:
I made three proposals in the `authoring` domain. All three came back with 0 issues. I changed nothing in `delivery`.

- **`objects.Element`:** I added an optional text property, `confirmation_note`, to hold the owner's reason for agreeing.
- **`actions.confirm_element`:** I added an optional `reason` parameter and an effect that stores it in `target.confirmation_note`. The person-only requirement, the kernel call and everything else are as before.
- **`actions.confirm_wording_element`:** I gave it the same optional `reason` parameter and the same effect, so both ways of confirming an element can carry a note. This goes slightly beyond `confirm_element`, but the request said "each confirmation".

The note is optional, so existing scenarios and confirmations keep working. I did not touch `confirm_all_proposed`. It confirms many elements at once and has no single reason to record. If you want a note there too, that is a separate change.

probes.answer:
I haven't answered the open question, because the answer has to come from you. The question is: "What must always be true about a Book, in every stage, however it got there?"

An answer is recorded in your words and becomes invariants in the library domain. I don't know the library's rules, so anything I wrote would be my invention under your name.

I sent you a message with three ways to move on:
- **Your own words:** give me a rule or two and I'll record them.
- **"Nothing":** say that no such rule exists and I'll record it.
- **Candidates:** I draft candidate invariants from the sources and you confirm or reject each one. I'd suggest this one if you're short on time.

I've made no changes to the draft, and I'll continue as soon as you reply.

messages_to_owner.text:
I can't decide this one for you. The open question is: "What must always be true about a Book, in every stage, however it got there? (If nothing, say so.)" Your answer would be recorded as your own words and would turn into invariants in the library domain. I don't know the library's rules, so I'd be inventing them. I've made no changes.

The quickest way forward is to reply with one of these:
1. A rule or two in your own words. Examples: "a checked-out book always has a borrower" or "a book is never both available and on loan".
2. "Nothing", if no such rule exists. I'll record that as your answer.
3. Tell me to propose candidate invariants for you to confirm or reject. I'd draft them from the sources, and you'd still confirm each one yourself.

I'd suggest option 3 if you're short on time.
choices: Propose candidates from the sources, I'll confirm
I'll answer in my own words
